summary.intent: Complete plan 65-06 of phase 65 (sdk-write-chain-bin-re-link-and-invite-claim) by implementing write-revocation cascade logic with a child-first rotation strategy.
summary.outcome: Successfully implemented `rotateWriteFromNode` and `rotateWriteSubtree` with `WriteRevocationCallbacks` type in the rotation engine; 8 new tests added, 70/70 rotation suite green, sdk-core 318 passed/22 skipped, build clean.

repo: Phase 65 uses a wave-based plan structure; wave 3 covered plans up to 65-06 (6/7 done), with plan 65-07 remaining as wave 4.
Write-revocation cascade is child-first — children are rotated before their parent node.
The rotation engine is in `packages/sdk-core/src/rotation/engine.ts` with a barrel re-export via `rotation/index.ts`.
Pre-commit hooks are slow enough to warrant extra time allocation when updating tracking files like ROADMAP.md.

code.finding: Added `WriteRevocationCallbacks` type, `rotateWriteFromNode` function, and `rotateWriteSubtree` function implementing child-first write-revocation cascade.
New 530-line test file with 8 tests covering the write-revocation driver contract.

workflow: Wave-based plan execution uses a build gate (typecheck) followed by a test gate before updating tracking; both gates must pass before committing to ROADMAP.md.
Executor is expected to stay out of STATE/ROADMAP files during plan execution — those are updated only by the orchestrator after gate checks pass.
Plans run on the main tree when no parallel file conflicts exist, avoiding worktree setup overhead.

friction: Slow pre-commit hooks required explicit extra time allowance when updating tracking files.
open_items: Plan 65-07 (wave 4, the final plan of phase 65) remains to be executed.
